[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Mastering GroupBy Operations and Aggregations in Pandas"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"The split-apply-combine pattern is fundamental to data analysis. In Pandas, this is achieved using the groupby() method. This tutorial covers how to group data, apply aggregate functions, and transform datasets efficiently."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Introduction to GroupBy"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Grouping data allows you to partition your DataFrame into smaller, manageable subsets based on one or more keys. Let us start by creating a sample dataset."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"import pandas as pd

data = {
    'Department': ['IT', 'HR', 'IT', 'HR', 'Sales', 'Sales'],
    'Employee': ['Alice', 'Bob', 'Charlie', 'David', 'Eve', 'Frank'],
    'Salary': [70000, 50000, 80000, 52000, 60000, 65000],
    'YearsExperience': [3, 2, 5, 3, 4, 6]
}
df = pd.DataFrame(data)
print(df)"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Basic Aggregations"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once the DataFrame is grouped, you can apply standard statistical functions such as mean(), sum(), min(), max(), and count()."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"# Calculate the average salary and experience by department
avg_stats = df.groupby('Department')[['Salary', 'YearsExperience']].mean()
print(avg_stats)"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Using the agg() Method for Multiple Functions"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"The agg() method allows you to apply multiple aggregation functions to one or more columns simultaneously. You can pass a list of functions or a dictionary mapping columns to specific functions."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"# Apply multiple aggregations using a dictionary
summary = df.groupby('Department').agg({
    'Salary': ['mean', 'max', 'min'],
    'YearsExperience': 'median'
})
print(summary)"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Custom Aggregations"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can also pass custom lambda functions or user-defined functions into the agg() method to perform complex calculations."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"# Calculate the salary range (max - min) for each department
salary_range = df.groupby('Department')['Salary'].agg(lambda x: x.max() - x.min())
print(salary_range)"},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"groupby() creates a DataFrameGroupBy object without computing anything until an aggregation is applied."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always select the subset of columns before applying aggregations to avoid performance overhead and type errors."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use named aggregations to cleanly rename columns during the agg() step."}]
